close_reason: Switched #[source] to #[from] on Other(E) variants of AvailabilityError and QueryCalendarEventsError. thiserror auto-generates From<E> impl; ? operator now works. Existing map_err call sites left as-is (tail-position .await.map_err return — converting to ? would require let-then-Ok and offers no readability gain). Future call sites get the ergonomic win.
description:
crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs:635 (AvailabilityError) and :709 (QueryCalendarEventsError) both define:

    pub enum XxxError<E: std::error::Error + 'static> {
        ...
        Other(#[source] E),
    }

Neither has a blanket `impl<E: std::error::Error + 'static> From<E> for XxxError<E>`. As a result, every backend implementation and every handler call site writes the same `.map_err(QueryCalendarEventsError::Other)` boilerplate:

- backend.rs:467 (the default `query_calendar_events` impl)
- lib.rs:802 (the test_support MockBackend impl)
- (every future production backend will write the same line)

A blanket `From` impl would let the `?` operator do the conversion automatically:

    impl<E: std::error::Error + 'static> From<E> for QueryCalendarEventsError<E> {
        fn from(e: E) -> Self { Self::Other(e) }
    }

This is a known Rust idiom for typed-error-with-source-passthrough enums; thiserror generates it automatically via `#[from]` annotation on the Other variant.

What callers cannot rely on:
- That the standard `?`-operator ergonomic works against these enums. They must remember to spell out the wrap.
- That the same enum from a sibling crate (which may or may not have the impl) behaves the same way.

The fix is `#[from]` instead of `#[source]` on the `Other` variant, OR explicit hand-rolled `From` impls. Compatible: the change does not break struct-literal `XxxError::Other(e)` callers and does not affect pattern-match exhaustiveness.

Sibling jmap-mail-server has no public error enums of this shape so there is no canonical to consult. Mirroring the precedent at jmap-jfia.36 (mail-server's BackendSetError lacks `From<E>` / `From<BackendSetError<E>>` for JmapError) — same defensive-forcing pattern across the workspace.

Mark with `opinion` if reviewer considers this a stylistic preference; the engineering basis is that `?`-operator support is the workspace-wide convention everywhere else (search for `#[from]` in the repo).
title: AvailabilityError::Other and QueryCalendarEventsError::Other lack From<E> impl; every caller writes .map_err(...::Other)
